rationale: Interpreted the successor receipt faa52ef8ac8a422aa26e12582959eda1, which executes the safety direction: in the new voter_promoted_after_snapshot shape the restarted node reconstructed one voter while its own log's committed configuration has two, became Leader without sending a single election request, and completed an Apply while the other member of the committed configuration was stopped; the flag-disabled control reconstructed the committed two-voter configuration, sought support from the other member and could neither lead nor commit. The two earlier divergences reproduced in the same run (comparisons 6 and 7 violated at parsed indices 4 and 10). Extended the reconstruction fact to this opposite divergence direction, added a fact for the minority-support consequence, and moved the discriminator to the still unexecuted lost-decision shape and the repair question.

investigations.discriminator: Whether an acknowledged commit that rested on a minority of the committed configuration is actually lost once a majority of the committed configuration that never held the entry forms new leadership (needs a committed configuration of three or more voters, where the reconstructed configuration is smaller), and whether any enabled path repairs a stale reconstruction without a later membership change.

knowledge.statement: A restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store reconstructs a configuration that is not the one recorded in the node's own log whenever the tracked commit index covers that node's last configuration entry, in both directions: the no-snapshot case reported latest_config_index 0 with no servers against a single-voter entry at log index 1; the snapshot-then-remove case reported latest_config_index 1 with the snapshot's two voters, one of them the peer removed at log index 103, against the single-voter entry there; and the snapshot-then-promote case reported latest_config_index 3 with a single voter, the promoted peer still carried as a nonvoter, against the two-voter entry at log index 104. The public GetConfiguration view reported the same value in each case, and the flag-disabled controls and the within-flag case whose configuration entry sits above the replayed prefix all reconstructed the configuration entry's own index and voter count.
knowledge.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores; RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the node's last configuration entry is either inside the applied prefix replayed from the tracked commit index (divergence, in either direction) or above it (correct reconstruction); no membership change is issued after the restart.
knowledge.changed_premise: The previous revision covered only the direction in which the reconstructed configuration had more voters than the committed one. This revision adds the opposite direction observed in receipt faa52ef8ac8a422aa26e12582959eda1, where the reconstructed configuration has fewer voters (one against two), which is the direction that changes which support suffices for an election and a commit.

knowledge.statement: In the retained promoted-voter execution, the reconstructed smaller configuration changed what support counted: the restarted instance became Leader while sending no election request at all (election_requests 0, became_leader true, state Leader) although the configuration entry in its own log has two voters, and a subsequent Apply completed (apply_ok true) while the other member of that committed configuration was stopped, so both the leadership decision and the committed decision rested on support from one of the two committed voters; the flag-disabled control over the same availability reported the two-voter configuration, sent 39 election requests, did not become leader, and its Apply failed with "node is not the leader".
knowledge.conditions: Two-member cluster whose committed configuration is a two-voter configuration recorded at log index 104 while the node's snapshot metadata still carries a single-voter configuration; every instance is stopped before the restart, the restarted instance is the only running member, and the commit attempt uses a 1000 ms Apply timeout.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt faa52ef8ac8a422aa26e12582959eda1 (completed, exit 0, TestAssuranceRestoreCommittedLogsContext passed, 21 parsed events) decides both parts of the question, including the direction in which the reconstructed configuration is smaller than the committed one. Reconstruction: comparison 0 is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 16, where the promoted-voter shape's restarted instance held latest_config_index 3 with one voter, the promoted peer still carried as a nonvoter, while its own log held the two-voter configuration entry at index 104; comparison 1 holds at parsed index 19, where the same restart with the flag disabled held latest_config_voters 2 equal to the log configuration entry. The earlier directions reproduce in the same run: comparison 6 is violated at parsed index 4 (no snapshot: no servers against the single-voter entry at index 1) and comparison 7 at parsed index 10 (snapshot-then-remove: the snapshot's two voters against the single-voter entry at index 103). Support consequences: comparison 2 holds at parsed index 17, where the flag-enabled instance became Leader (state_after_wait Leader, became_leader true) with election_requests 0, so it acquired authority without asking any member for a vote even though its own log's committed configuration has two voters; comparison 3 holds at parsed index 20, where the flag-disabled control tried to gather support (39 election requests) and stayed Candidate; comparison 5 holds at parsed index 20 with apply_ok false ("node is not the leader"), while comparison 4 holds at parsed index 17 with apply_ok true, so the commit completed with the other member of the committed two-voter configuration stopped and therefore without any second copy. Together these show a leadership decision and an acknowledged commit resting on support from one of the two committed voters, which the committed configuration does not permit: quorumSize and the leader commitment were computed from the reconstructed smaller configuration [candidate_quorum, quorum_size, leader_commitment, commitment_impl], and the reconstruction is the startup scan skipping the committed configuration entry [scan_start, restore_lastapplied]. Superseded: the earlier interpretation's open safety direction is now exercised for a two-voter committed configuration and moved from source-only to observed; its measurements for the other shapes are independently reproduced by this receipt at parsed indices 4 and 10. Still open: the acknowledged entry's fate when a majority of the committed configuration that never held it forms new leadership, which needs a committed configuration of three or more voters and is captured as the current discriminator; and the repair question, which remains answered only from source.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces the divergence and the non-progress: excluded in the previous receipt by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix (comparisons holding there with the flag enabled), and this receipt's flag-disabled controls hold the same configurations and refuse the same decisions.

Limits of the exercised consequence: the new shape stops every instance before the restart, so the stale leader is not contested by a live majority and the receipt establishes which support the decisions rested on, not an observed competing leader or an observed lost entry.
limitations: The bounded observations use one process with in-memory stores and a 3000 ms leadership window plus a 1000 ms commit timeout; they are not an unbounded liveness or durability proof.

The lost-decision consequence is not exercised: with a committed configuration of exactly two voters no other majority can elect without the entry, so an acknowledged entry that rests on one copy cannot yet be shown to be discarded.
Not exercised: disk-backed commit-tracking stores, crashes during the restart, restarted peers rejoining after the acknowledged commit, and post-restart membership changes or snapshot installs.
Only the demote/snapshot/promote ladder and the remove-after-snapshot shapes were exercised; skip windows produced by longer committed sequences were not varied.
